name: District of Columbia
agency: District of Columbia Department of Motor Vehicles (DC DMV)
permitAge: 16 (learner permit; all new drivers of any age start with a learner permit)

teen.supervisedHours: 40 hours before the provisional license (form DMV-GRAD-HR40); 10 more hours at night during the provisional stage before the full license with conditions (secondary)
teen.holdPermit: 6 months (secondary); waived for applicants who turn 21 while holding the permit
teen.nightLimit: Learner permit: 6 a.m. to 9 p.m. only. Provisional (secondary): Sept-June Sun-Thu 6 a.m.-10:59 p.m., Fri-Sat 6 a.m.-11:59 p.m.; July-Aug every day 6 a.m.-11:59 p.m.; exceptions for work, school, religious or athletic events, or with a licensed driver 21+
teen.phone: All drivers: hand-held phone use banned while moving, hands-free allowed. Learner permit holders and school bus drivers: no phone at all, hands-free included, except emergency calls (secondary, 2004 law).

notes: Knowledge test question count and pass mark not found on an official page; commercial sites disagree (25 questions / 20 to pass, or 30 / 24). Both are 80 percent. Left null.
Knowledge test offered in 15 languages including Spanish (DC DMV press release, undated).
DC driver manual URL (English or Spanish) not found within the search budget.
Default speed limit 20 mph since June 1, 2020 (DDOT); 15 mph next to schools at signed times.
Right turn on red: Safer Streets Amendment Act banned it from Jan 1, 2025, but news reports say it is enforced only where No Turn on Red signs are posted. Not used in questions.
Provisional passenger limits exist but the exact rule was not found. Left null.
School bus: on undivided roads both directions stop (secondary); not state-specific enough for a question.
